title: Getting started with Wistudi
text: If someone has invited you to a lesson, start with their link. If you want to explore or publish, sign in and use Discover or your publishing workspace. Choose your starting point You do not need to build anything to take part in learning. Start with the task you came to do: Complete a lesson: open the link from your teacher, trainer or publisher. Follow the invitation and sign-in instructions on that page. Explore learning: open Discover to browse available XP Videos and Flows. Create learning: use the XP Videos or Flows area of your publishing workspace. Begin with one short lesson rather than a complete course. Attend an event: use the event's registration or joining link. Event registration and access to a separate lesson are different actions; follow the instructions supplied by your host. Create or access your account Open Create an account . If you already have an account, choose Sign In instead. For email registration, enter your first name, last name, email address and password, then choose Create Account . Use an email inbox you can access. Look for the verification email and follow its link. If it is missing, check spam or junk and use Resend verification email on the verification screen. Complete any profile or onboarding requirements shown in your account. If you arrived through an invitation, return to the original invitation link after signing in. Account creation does not give access to every private lesson, organisation or event. Access still depends on the invitation, account permissions and the content's availability. Understand XP Videos and Flows An XP Video adds activities and checkpoints to a video. A checkpoint can ask you to answer, reflect or complete a task while watching. A Flow brings pages, content and activities into a learning sequence. It can combine explanations, videos, questions and resources in one experience. If you are learning, follow the instructions and requirements displayed in the experience. If you are publishing, choose the format that fits the learning: video-led learning suits an XP Video; a sequence of mixed content suits a Flow. If part of the platform is locked Some navigation areas have onboarding requirements. Read the requirement shown beside the locked section and use its action to continue. Do not create another account to try to unlock it. A message that your account or content has restricted access needs a different response: return to your invitation, contact the person who shared the content, or ask Wistudi Support. See Dashboard and workspaces for help choosing the right area.

title: Your account and profile
text: Use your own account and an email address you can access. My Profile is for your profile; Account Settings is for account preferences. Review visibility before sharing a profile. Register with an email you control Open the registration page . Enter your first name, last name, email address and password in the fields shown. Review the information and choose Create Account . Open the verification email and follow the link to confirm your email address. Continue to sign in and complete the profile or onboarding steps shown. If you already have an account, use Sign In . Creating another account can leave invitations, learning and published work associated with different identities. Independent registration is for users aged 16 or over. Younger learners need an approved supervised arrangement. A parent, guardian or authorised organisation should contact Wistudi if they need help arranging access. Verify your email address Verification confirms that you can access the email address on your account. Check that the address displayed on the verification screen is correct, then look in your inbox and spam or junk folder. Use Resend verification email if needed. If a verification link is invalid or expired, choose Request a new link and use the newly issued email. Copying only part of the URL can prevent it from working. Never send your verification link or password to another person. Support may ask for your account email and the error message, but does not need your password. Find your profile and settings Open your account menu and look for My Profile or Account Settings . My Profile: view your profile and the editing options available to you. Review your display information before sharing your profile. Account Settings: manage the account preferences and settings available for your account. Profile setup: if onboarding asks you to complete your profile, follow that prompt. You can also open profile settings while signed in. After editing, use the save or confirmation control shown and check that the update succeeds before leaving. A setting labelled Coming soon is not a promise that the associated service is active. Understand visibility and protect your account Your public profile and your private account records are different. Profile information may be displayed according to your visibility and publishing settings; that does not make private learner progress, assessments or transactions public. Only include contact details or personal information you intend to share in a public profile. Review the Privacy Policy for how Wistudi handles personal information. Keep your password private, use a password you do not reuse elsewhere, and sign out on a shared device. If you no longer control the account email or suspect someone else has accessed your account, contact support@wistudi.com before creating a replacement account.

title: Sign-in and account recovery
text: Use the email address and sign-in method connected to your account. For a forgotten password, choose Forgot your password? and request a reset link. Sign in to the correct account Open Sign In . For email sign-in, enter your account email and password, then choose Sign In . If you registered using Google, use the Google sign-in option with the same Google account. Complete any verification or account prompts shown. If you are trying to open shared learning, return to the original invitation link after signing in. Check for typing mistakes and unwanted spaces in your email address. If you use more than one email or Google account, make sure you are using the identity that received the invitation or owns the work you need. Reset a forgotten password On the sign-in page, choose Forgot your password? , or open password recovery . Enter your account email address and choose Send Reset Link . Open the reset email and follow the complete link. Enter your new password in New Password and repeat it in Confirm New Password . Choose Reset Password . Once the success message appears, return to sign-in and use your new password. Follow the password requirements shown by the form. If the link is invalid, expired or missing its reset token, choose Request a new link and use the new email. Do not forward a reset link to anyone else. If an account email has not arrived Check that the email address you entered is correct and that you can receive mail in that inbox. Look in spam, junk and any filtered mail folders. Use Resend reset link or Resend verification email on the relevant screen. Open the message for the action you just requested. An email-verification link and a password-reset link have different purposes. If the message still does not arrive, contact support with your account email, the action you requested and the approximate time. Do not include your password or a full reset or verification link. If your account is restricted or suspended A password reset does not remove an account restriction. If Wistudi displays a suspension or access message, read the explanation and contact your organisation's administrator or Wistudi Support as appropriate. Include the exact message and the email address on your account. Avoid creating another account to bypass a restriction; it can separate your learning and content from the original account. If you cannot access the email inbox linked to your account, ask support for help. Do not assume a new account can inherit your previous content or records.

title: Dashboard and workspaces
text: Use Discover to find learning, My Learning Library to return to lessons and Publishing Workspace to create or manage your own content. Choose the area for your task Wistudi separates exploring, learning and publishing in the navigation. These are different views of your work, so a lesson you are taking and a lesson you are editing may appear in different places. Discover: explore available XP Videos and Flows. My Learning Library: return to video and Flow lessons associated with your learning. My Progress: view the learning progress available for your account. Publishing Workspace: find the XP Videos and Flows areas for creating, editing and managing your own content. My Profile and Account Settings: use the account menu for your profile and account preferences. Some navigation labels and options depend on the account and workspace you are using. A creator or administrator may see controls that a learner does not. Return to a lesson Sign in with the account you used when you started the lesson or received the invitation. Open My Learning Library and look for the lesson title. If you cannot find it, open the original invitation or assignment link. Follow the access message or the lesson's start or continue action. Do not use a creator's editing workspace as a shortcut to a learner assignment. The original invitation is the best starting point when you are unsure which content was shared with you. Find your publishing work For content you own or help manage, open the appropriate XP Videos or Flows area in Publishing Workspace . Check the title and content type before editing. If your account offers a workspace selector, check that the intended personal or organisation workspace is selected. A change of workspace can change the content and permissions you see. Do not create a duplicate lesson until you have checked the account and workspace. Understand locked navigation Some sections unlock through onboarding. The navigation can show requirements such as completing a profile, choosing learning preferences, or creating content. Expand the locked section and read its requirements. Use the action shown for the requirement you want to complete. Finish and save the requested setup, then return to the navigation. Completing onboarding does not grant organisation permissions or access to someone else's private content. If an access restriction remains, contact the person who invited you or support with the message you see.

title: Find and access learning
text: Open the original lesson link and follow its access instructions. A private link can have restrictions, and signing in does not automatically grant access to every lesson. Open a shared lesson or invitation Use the complete link supplied by your teacher, trainer or publisher. Check the title and creator on the invitation or content page. If asked, choose Sign In or create an account. Use the account intended for the invitation. After signing in or finishing account setup, return to the original link if the lesson has not reopened. Choose the start or continue action displayed and read the lesson instructions before beginning. If your teacher sent a replacement link, use that link rather than an older bookmark. Do not publish a private invitation link in a public group or on social media. Find learning without an invitation Use Discover to explore content available there. If you have already started a lesson, look in My Learning Library or return to its original link. Private or assigned content does not have to appear in Discover. If you cannot find a lesson in search, ask the person who shared it for the correct access link instead of looking for a similar title. Understand guest access Some shared experiences offer Continue as Guest ; others require sign-in. The choices shown depend on the content and its sharing settings. Guest progress can be limited to the browser session, and features such as saved account progress or reports may be unavailable. If the learning is an assignment or your teacher needs a recorded result, sign in with the intended account before starting. Do not assume work completed as a guest will transfer to your account later. A preview or guest view is not the same as being enrolled or having full learner access. Follow the invitation's instructions if it asks you to sign in. If the lesson will not open Sign-in required: sign in, then reopen the original invitation. Wrong account or workspace: check the signed-in email and the intended workspace where available. Invalid, expired or access-limit message: ask the sender to check the link and provide new access if appropriate. Repeated refreshing does not renew a link. Content unavailable: the publisher may need to check its publication or sharing settings. Ask them before assuming it is a device problem. Locked pages or activities: read the requirements shown in the lesson. Access to one page does not necessarily mean every page is open. If the issue continues, send support the content title, page link and exact message. Send private links only to the sender or support, and do not include passwords or reset links.

title: Troubleshooting
text: First record the error and protect unsaved work. Then check the account, link, connection and browser. Contact support with the affected page and the steps that reproduce the problem. Before refreshing or closing the page If you are writing a response or editing content, keep a copy of text you have not successfully saved or submitted. Check the save or submission message before leaving. Record the exact error, the content title and what you were doing when the problem occurred. A screenshot of the error is helpful, but crop or hide unrelated personal or learner information. Do not repeatedly confirm publishing, payment or submission actions while the result is unclear. Check whether the action completed first. If a credit balance or payment looks wrong, contact support with the transaction context rather than trying the same purchase again. A page or video will not load Check whether other pages load on the same connection. After protecting unsaved work, reload the affected page. Try the page in an updated browser. If needed, compare with another browser or a private window to check whether an extension or browser setting is involved. If only one video fails, note whether it is an external video and copy the exact player message. A source video can become unavailable independently of Wistudi. If the platform displays a desktop-only notice, use a desktop or laptop browser and reopen the original link. A private window may require you to sign in again. Do not clear browser storage or cookies as your first step: it can remove local session information and sign you out. A lesson is locked or progress looks wrong For an access message, check the original invitation and the account you are signed into. An expired link, access limit or permission restriction needs the sender or administrator to review it; changing browsers will not grant permission. If progress or a result appears missing, check that you are using the same account and the same lesson. Note whether you completed the work as a guest, in a preview or while signed in. Record the activity name, approximate completion time and any confirmation you saw. Do not restart an assessed activity just to test whether the record changes. Ask your teacher or support to review it if another attempt could affect your result. Saving or publishing did not finish Keep the page open while you check its status. Look for validation messages, required settings or a clear save confirmation. If the connection dropped, preserve unsaved text before retrying. If a publishing action appears to have used credits but did not complete, send the content title, approximate time and error to support. Do not delete the content to try to reverse the action; deletion is not a credit-restoration request. The Credit Usage Policy explains how verified technical errors are reviewed. Send a useful support report Email support@wistudi.com or use the support enquiry form . Include: Your account email and whether you were signed in or using guest access. The page link, content title and affected activity. What you expected, what happened, and the steps to reproduce it. The approximate date, time and timezone. Your device, browser and the exact error message. A screenshot if it helps explain the problem. Never send passwords, reset links, verification codes or full payment-card details. Share private content links only with the authorised sender or support.

title: Create an XP Video
description: Add a video, place activity checkpoints, configure the learner experience and prepare your XP Video for publishing.
text: Add a source video to your workspace, choose Create Interactive Lesson or Make Interactive, then use Add Activity Checkpoint at the moment you want learners to respond. Start with the learning purpose Choose a video that supports one clear learning goal. Decide where a learner needs to do something with what they have watched: recall a detail, make a choice, sort examples or explain an idea. Put a checkpoint near the relevant moment rather than collecting every question at the end. For example, pause a demonstration after a key step and ask learners to identify what should happen next. Use only videos you own or have permission to use. An external video remains dependent on its source and embedding permissions. Add your video Sign in and open the XP Video Workspace in your publishing area. Choose Upload Video to open the Add Video flow. Choose Upload Video for a file, or External URL for a supported YouTube or Vimeo link. Follow the upload or Fetch Video Details steps. Review the required title, category, topic and other fields shown. Save the source video, then choose Create Interactive Lesson . For a source already in your workspace, use Make Interactive where offered. A saved source video is not automatically an interactive lesson. You still need to add and configure the activities. See Videos, uploads and resources if the source cannot be added. Add and configure checkpoints Play or seek to the relevant timestamp in the video. Choose Add Activity Checkpoint and select an available activity type. Write the prompt and any learner instructions. Add the questions, options or activity items required by that type. Set the correct answers and relevant feedback or grading options. Save the activity and repeat at other learning moments. If an activity already exists at the timestamp, select that checkpoint to work on it. Do not add an empty checkpoint as a placeholder and expect it to pass publication checks. Choose each activity for its purpose. A quick question checks understanding; sorting or matching asks learners to apply a relationship; a written response needs a clear prompt and, when graded, a marking approach. Review playback and assessment settings Open Activity Playback Settings and review the controls available for progression, navigation, attempts, retakes and the video pass mark. Check the Lesson Rules summary to see how these choices affect the learner. Sequential learning asks learners to complete activities in order and can restrict skipping ahead. Open navigation and retake choices change how learners practise. Use the settings displayed in the current interface rather than assuming every activity has independent controls. Preview, save and publish Use Preview Learner View once the lesson has enough complete content to preview. Check checkpoint timing, instructions, answers and the route back to playback. Preview is for checking the experience; share a learner link for actual participation. Use Save Draft and confirm that the save succeeded. If saving is disabled, read the message about empty activities, missing prompts or incomplete questions. Review Publishing Requirements before choosing Publish . Requirements can vary with video length, and all activities must be configured. Review any credit confirmation before proceeding. After publication succeeds, use Share to obtain learner access.

title: Create a Flow
description: Build a learning sequence with pages, collections, content and activities, then configure, preview and publish it.
text: Open Flow Workspace, choose New Flow, select an available starting structure and build your learning sequence with pages and blocks. Complete Flow Settings before publishing. Outline the learning sequence A Flow brings explanations, media, activities and assessment into one learning experience. Start with what learners should understand or be able to do, then sketch the steps that will help them get there. A short sequence might introduce the topic, show an example, ask learners to practise and finish with reflection. Use collections when a larger experience needs clear groups of pages. Create the Flow in your workspace Sign in and open Flow Workspace . Choose New Flow or the Create Flow action in an empty workspace. Enter a descriptive Flow Name and complete the category and topic fields shown. Review Choose Your Starting Structure and select an available option. Continue with the creation action shown to open your Flow. Single Flow describes pages directly inside the Flow. Structured Flow organises content using collections and pages. A choice marked as unavailable or coming soon cannot be used yet; select an available structure. Choose the organisation you need before building a large amount of content. Organise pages and collections Use the structure navigation and Add New Content controls to add the pages or collections supported by your Flow. Add Page creates a page under the selected Flow or collection; Add Collection creates a grouping within the Flow. Name each page for its learning purpose. Select the page you want to edit before adding content. Arrange the pages in a useful learning order. Keep related pages together in a collection when the structure supports it. Workspace collections used to organise your library are different from collections inside a Flow's learning structure. Moving a Flow into a workspace collection does not build its internal sequence. Build the pages with blocks Add content blocks for explanation and examples, then activity blocks for the learner's response. Set the instructions, media, answers and grading options available for each block. A page should have a clear purpose. Avoid squeezing unrelated activities together just to reduce page count. Check the page layout and any space or placement warnings in the builder. For example, use a short explanation and example to introduce a concept, then a sorting activity to check how learners classify new examples. See Blocks and activities for guidance on choosing interactions. Complete Flow Settings Open Configure Flow or Flow Settings . Review the required fields under General Info , Content & Identity and Visuals & Branding . Use a clear description, learning outcomes, appropriate trainer information and representative visuals. Follow any remaining required-settings messages, then choose Save & Exit . If you use an AI-assisted fill action, review its output before saving. You are responsible for the accuracy of descriptions, outcomes and images. Preview and prepare to release Preview the learner experience from the builder. Read it in order and try the activities, including incorrect answers where appropriate. Check that instructions, media and completion requirements make sense together. Save your draft and review the publishing confirmation. Workspace publication and a public Discover listing are separate states: a workspace version can be published while a Discover submission is still under review. Read Publish, update and manage versions before releasing the Flow, then use the learner sharing controls when access is ready.

title: Blocks and activities
description: Choose blocks for a learning goal, configure the learner task and check answers, feedback and grading before publication.
text: Choose a block for what the learner needs to do, then configure the prompt, response and assessment. Preview the interaction before publishing it. Choose by learning purpose Start with the learner's action, not the longest feature list. A block is useful when it helps someone understand, practise, explain or demonstrate something. Explain or demonstrate: use text, images, video or a supporting document. Check a specific answer: consider Multiple Choice, True / False or Picture Quiz. Connect ideas: use Link & Match for pairs and relationships. Classify examples: use Smart Sorting when learners need to distinguish categories. Order a process: use Sequence & Reorder when order is the learning goal. Explain thinking: use Written Response or a reflection activity with a clear prompt. Collect a view: use Community Poll when you want a response or discussion starter rather than a single correct answer. The block menu is the source of available choices. Some blocks belong to a particular builder or can be unavailable for your account. A block marked Coming soon is not ready to add. Add the block in the right place In a Flow, select the page you are editing and open its block-adding controls. In an XP Video, select a timestamp, choose Add Activity Checkpoint and select an available activity. Place the task close to the explanation or media it depends on. If a block depends on information from a previous page or video section, make that connection clear in the instructions. Configure the task completely Write a prompt that tells learners what to do and what information to use. Add the items needed by the activity: answer options, category labels, matching pairs, ordered items or a response prompt. Set the correct answers or intended order where the block uses automatic checking. Check image readability, captions and any supporting resources. Review the feedback and response settings available for that block. Save and resolve any missing-content warnings. A short instruction such as “Match each term to its meaning” is more useful than a decorative title with no task. Keep prompts understandable without the teacher needing to explain the interface separately. Decide how the response is assessed Separate practising from being assessed. Review the block's available grading controls and any overall lesson rules before deciding what should affect a result. For automatically checked activities, verify the answer configuration. For a graded written response, provide an appropriate marking guide and points using the controls offered. A poll should not be presented as a knowledge test unless the activity actually supports that assessment. Settings can operate at different levels. XP Video attempt and progression rules may be controlled in the video settings, while a block can have its own response or feedback options. Do not assume a field on one block exists on every other block. Test before publishing Preview the activity as a learner. Try the expected response and a plausible mistake. Check whether feedback appears when intended and whether the learner can continue, retry or submit as the lesson requires. For manual responses, check that instructions and assessment criteria agree. If a supporting file is required, make that requirement clear before the learner starts. If a block is unavailable or publication is blocked, read the specific requirement in the builder. Some eligible actions or advanced options can depend on credits; review the confirmation shown rather than assuming all blocks have the same publishing treatment.

title: Videos, uploads and resources
description: Add uploaded files and supported external video links, preserve attribution, and resolve media or resource problems.
text: Use the supported upload or external-link option, review the file or source details and test the resource in preview. External media must remain available at its original source. Choose an upload or an external video In the video-adding flow, Upload Video adds a file from your device. External URL adds an individual video from a supported source such as YouTube or Vimeo. Use an upload when you have a suitable file and the rights to publish it. Use an external URL when you want to use an eligible video hosted by the source platform. Adding a link does not transfer ownership of that video or guarantee that it will always remain available. Upload a video file Open the video-adding flow from your workspace and choose Upload Video . Select Choose File or use the drop area. Follow the formats and size limit displayed for your account. MP4 and WebM are supported upload options; if your file is rejected, follow the specific validation message. Wait for the upload to finish before continuing. Review the title, description, category, topic and other required details. Save the video and check the success message before closing the flow. Changing a file extension does not convert its format. If a MOV or another unsupported file is rejected, export or convert a separate copy into a supported format and keep your original file. Upload limits can depend on the current account configuration. Use the limit shown in the uploader rather than relying on a limit quoted in an older guide. Add a YouTube or Vimeo link Choose External URL and select the source platform. Paste the complete video URL into the matching field. Choose Fetch Video Details . Review the retrieved video and complete the remaining required classification fields. Save, then preview the video before adding or publishing learning around it. For external sources, the title, description and thumbnail can be supplied by the source platform and locked against editing. Preserve the source attribution and channel or original-video links shown by Wistudi. Do not use an unauthorised downloaded copy to work around embedding restrictions. A video that is private, removed, region-restricted or unavailable for embedding may not play for your learners. Add supporting media and resources Use the content or resource controls available in the selected Flow block or activity to add images, video, PDFs or links. The options depend on the block; not every activity accepts every type of attachment. Use descriptive names and captions so learners know why a resource matters. Make sure the text in an image or PDF remains readable at the size learners will see. Check the permission settings of external documents separately. A resource being visible to you while signed in to its source service does not prove that learners can open it. Test the learner link and arrange appropriate access with the resource owner. If media does not work Upload rejected: check the actual file format and the account limit shown. Details cannot be fetched: check the selected platform and complete URL. Video plays for you but not learners: check the source's visibility, embedding and regional restrictions. Resource asks for permission: review the permissions at the external service. Preview shows the wrong file: check that you selected the intended page or block before replacing anything. If the problem continues, contact support with the content title, affected resource and exact message. Do not send private learner work or credentials unless specifically needed through an authorised support route.

title: Publish, update and manage versions
description: Check publishing requirements, distinguish workspace publication from Discover review, and prepare updates without confusing existing learners.
text: Save and preview your content, complete the publishing requirements and review the confirmation. For Flows, workspace publication, Discover listing and template review are separate states. Check the content before publishing Save your draft, preview the learner experience and resolve the requirements shown in the builder. Confirm the title, instructions, answer configuration and resources before release. XP Videos: review Publishing Requirements . The activity requirement varies with video length, and checkpoints and questions must be configured. Flows: open Configure Flow and finish the required General Info , Content & Identity and Visuals & Branding fields. Use Save & Exit and resolve any remaining content warnings. Saving a draft and publishing are different actions. A successful save does not mean a learner can already open the content. Publish a Flow to your workspace Choose Publish when the builder requirements are complete. Review the Publish Flow confirmation and its available publishing options. Check the intended visibility and whether you are also requesting a Discover listing or submitting a template. Review the credit summary, included output and any acknowledgements. Confirm publication only when you are ready, then wait for the success message. Workspace publication makes a published version available in your own workspace. It does not by itself mean the Flow is publicly listed in Discover. Template submission has separate reuse permissions and acknowledgements. Do not select it simply to obtain a learner link. Read the Template Publishing & Remix Terms before granting reuse rights. Understand Discover review A Flow can be published in your workspace while a Discover submission is still under review. Use the available Discover publishing option or Available in Discover in configuration when you want to request a listing. Check Review Status and the feedback shown. In Review is not approval. If changes are requested, address the reasons and required actions before resubmitting. Where offered, Recall Submission cancels the pending review so you can edit again. A live, approved listing can have different controls: if the interface requires an administrator to remove it, contact an administrator rather than treating it as a normal draft. XP Video publishing uses its own status and confirmation. Read the video interface directly instead of assuming the Flow review process applies unchanged. Edit with existing learners in mind Before editing published content, check its current version, learners and review status. The available action can be Edit , Update , Edit Draft or Create New Version . In Manage Flow Versions , a new editable version is a draft copy. Creating that draft does not itself replace the current learner experience. Learners stay on their existing version while you prepare the update. If there are no enrolled learners, the interface may offer direct editing of the published version. An existing draft, a pending review or a live Discover listing can restrict the options. Follow the explanation shown for that Flow. Before publishing updates, review how they affect the current release and any review requirements. Do not assume that changing answers, points or assessed tasks has the same effect as correcting explanatory text. Check the confirmation and ask support before a change that could affect an active assessment. Review credit confirmations Publishing pages, eligible videos, new versions or selected advanced options can use credits. Review the total and any breakdown displayed before confirming. Use the amount shown in the confirmation for your action, as costs depend on what you publish. If publication appears to fail after credits were deducted, keep the content and note the time and error. Do not repeatedly confirm the action or delete the content to try to restore credits. Contact support and refer to the Credit Usage Policy . Check access after publication Open the published item from the workspace, check its status and obtain a learner link through Share . Test the intended access route before distributing it widely. Archiving, moving to trash, deleting, removing a Discover listing and deleting a draft version are different actions. Read the confirmation for the action you choose; do not use deletion as a shortcut to hide or update content used by learners.

title: Share content and control access
description: Choose learner sharing links, configure expiry and access limits, and understand guest access and link regeneration.
text: Use Share or Share with Learners on published content. Choose the available learner link, review its access settings and copy it after the settings have saved. Share the learner experience Open the published Flow or XP Video in your workspace and choose Share or Share with Learners . Use the resulting learner link, not the builder URL or a creator preview URL. A preview is intended for checking content. Learners should use the invitation or access link designed for participation so they receive the correct access instructions. Before sharing, decide who needs access, whether the link should stop accepting new learners after a date, and whether an access limit is appropriate. Choose an available link type The sharing panel depends on the content and its publication state. A public link can be unavailable when the content is not on Discover; that does not necessarily mean the workspace version failed to publish. Public Link: use it when the panel makes it available and you intend the linked content to be accessible to that audience. Temporary Link: on a Flow, generate a controlled link and review the expiry and access settings shown. Private Access Link: on interfaces that offer it, use the protected link and its access controls. If public sharing is unavailable, use the permitted controlled-link option rather than turning on a public listing just to bypass the access setting. Discover visibility and learner link management are different decisions. Generate, save and copy a link Open the sharing panel on the intended published content or version. Review the available link and its active, inactive or expired status. Set an Expiry Date and Access Limit where offered. Read whether settings apply immediately or when the link is generated. Choose Generate Link if a link does not yet exist. Use the displayed save action when settings require saving. Wait for the saved or generated confirmation, then choose Copy . Test the copied learner link before sending it to your audience. An access limit controls new use of that link. If the limit has been reached, review the setting or ask for help rather than repeatedly sending the same unavailable invitation. Where share-to-service buttons are offered, check which URL they will use. A Flow can use its Temporary Link when a public link is unavailable. The destination service may have its own account and posting requirements. Understand regeneration and expiry Regenerate is not the same as copying the current link. The current sharing interface warns that regeneration can make the old link inactive. For Flow temporary links, the confirmation explains that the current link stops working for people who have not opened it yet, while learners who already joined keep their access. Read that confirmation before proceeding. If you issue a replacement link, update the invitation or message that your audience will use. Expiry or deactivation can prevent future access through a link. Do not assume it deletes earlier submissions, removes every learner relationship or reverses an assignment. Check the settings and contact support if you need to change access for people who already joined. Understand guest and signed-in access The invitation can offer Continue as Guest , require sign-in or restrict access according to the content's settings. Do not promise guest access unless it is offered on the actual link. Guest progress may be limited to the browser session, and recorded learning features may be unavailable. When you need an identifiable learner record or assessment history, instruct the learner to sign in with the intended account before starting. Tell recipients to use the complete link and return to it after sign-in if necessary. See Find and access learning for the learner-facing instructions. Check before sending to a group Confirm the lesson title, version and access settings. Open the learner link in a separate signed-out browser session to see the invitation state, without completing an attempt that could use a limited access slot. If the link reports unavailable, expired or an access limit, check the publisher's settings first. Send private links only to the intended recipients. A link that works for you as the owner is not proof that every recipient has permission.

title: Using Zoom with Wistudi
description: Connect Zoom, run live classes with a Flow in Training Rooms, and disconnect the app when you no longer need it.
text: Connect your Zoom account in My Space → Training Rooms, create a room with a Flow, and share the room link with your learners. Requirements A Wistudi account. A Zoom account. A free Zoom account normally ends meetings after 40 minutes; a paid Zoom licence is recommended for classes. See Zoom’s meeting time limits . A desktop browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Add the app Sign in to Wistudi and open My Space → Training Rooms . Click Connect Zoom . Sign in to Zoom and click Allow . The Training Rooms page now shows your Zoom account as connected. Use the app In My Space → Training Rooms , click Create Training Room . Choose a Flow, enter a name and choose when the room is open. Copy the room link and send it to your learners. Click Enter . Zoom starts inside Wistudi and the Flow is shown next to the video. Learners open the link, sign in to Wistudi and join the meeting. They can join only while the host is in the meeting. When the class is over, click End room . The Zoom meeting ends for everyone. Remove the app You can remove the connection from either Wistudi or Zoom: In Wistudi: open My Space → Training Rooms → Disconnect Zoom . In Zoom: sign in at marketplace.zoom.us , then open Manage → Added Apps → Wistudi → Remove . If your Zoom Marketplace shows My Library instead, find Wistudi there and choose Remove from its actions menu. See Zoom’s app removal instructions . When the app is removed, Wistudi deletes your stored Zoom tokens. Existing Training Rooms can no longer start until you connect Zoom again.
